new_entities.name: Tongue-strengthening myofunctional therapy
aliases: tongue exercises for obstructive sleep apnea
new_entities.description: Tongue-focused or oropharyngeal myofunctional exercise programs intended to improve upper-airway muscle function in obstructive sleep apnea.

new_entities.name: Reduction in apnea-hypopnea index
new_entities.description: A reduction in the apnea-hypopnea index, indicating fewer obstructive breathing events during sleep.

edges.effect_quant: The literature is conflicted. A 2025 re-analysis of systematic reviews found mean AHI improvement of -9.54 events/h, but two newer randomized trials of tongue-focused or combined myofunctional programs found no significant between-group AHI benefit.
edges.population: adults with mild to moderate obstructive sleep apnea, especially patients seeking non-device adjunctive therapy
edges.mechanism: These exercises aim to improve tone and coordination of the tongue and pharyngeal dilator muscles, which could reduce airway collapse during sleep if the targeted muscle dysfunction is a key driver of disease.
edges.summary: Myofunctional therapy remains plausible and sometimes promising, but the newer trial-level signal is inconsistent and seems weaker than the more optimistic pooled literature suggests.
edges.caveats: Many studies are small, heterogeneous, and at high risk of bias. Results may differ between multi-component myofunctional programs and narrow tongue-only protocols, and durable objective AHI improvement is uncertain.

evidence.citation: PisoniE et al 2025 J Sleep Res
evidence.notes: Myofunctional Therapy in Adults and Children With Obstructive Sleep Apnea: An Overview and Re-Analysis of Systematic Reviews.

effect_quant.comparator: AHI with myofunctional therapy versus control in adults
